processing: The globe-shaped flower heads are dried whole and steeped in boiling water. Their papery bracts keep their colour after drying, which is the reason for the name.
harvest_season: Little is documented about harvest for tea; the dried flowers sell year-round.
appearance_dry: Round, papery flower heads the size of a large marble, vivid magenta to purple-red.
appearance_liquor: Clear with a pink to rosy red tint, typical of red-flowered infusions.
appearance_wet: Soft round heads that keep their shape and shed some of their colour.
taste_profile: Usually described as gently sweet and floral, light on the tongue; little specific tasting detail is documented.

brewing.notes: Three to five heads in a glass with boiling water. It suits a glass cup, where the colour shows, and blends easily with other flowers.

vintage_note: Sold by weight as dried whole flowers with no vintage, like most Chinese flower teas. Colour holds for a long time, so a bright look does not prove freshness; judge by clean smell and intact heads. It also appears as a component of blooming display teas, which are a different product with a tea base.
description:
Qian Ri Hong, thousand-day red, is the dried flower head of globe amaranth. It is sold in Chinese flower-tea shops largely for one reason: it keeps its striking magenta long after drying.

There is little to the making. The papery bracts dry whole and hold their colour, which also makes the plant popular for dried arrangements.

Steeped in boiling water it gives a sweet, mellow, gently floral cup. It is not strong, so a tall glass and a few heads will show it off better than a small pot. Blend it with other flowers if you want more flavour.

Buying is mostly about cleanliness. Choose whole, unbroken heads with no musty smell. If you see it inside a tied blooming tea, that drink is built on tea leaves and is not the same thing.
history: Little is documented about qian ri hong as a drink, and no reliable date for its use as tea is on record. Today it is sold in Chinese herbal and flower-tea ranges.
